limitations: Retrieval budget for this work unit was capped at 5 web searches; evidence collection used 3 targeted queries plus confirmatory follow-up, consistent with the single-search-route depth applied to comparable languages in this evaluation family.

Scores reflect a frozen author-defined weighted checklist rubric rather than a single external benchmark; the checklist and weights are recorded above so the same rubric can be reapplied unchanged to the other 9 languages.

deduction_citations: <cite index="1-12,1-13">The command brew install openjdk@25 installs a Homebrew-managed build, and this approach requires manual symlink configuration before macOS can discover it.</cite>
<cite index="5-17,5-18">Installing via brew install openjdk@8 was noted to be several point releases behind, i.e. lagging the upstream Adoptium build.</cite>

items: Homebrew formula installs require manual symlink configuration before macOS system tools discover the JDK, and Homebrew's own OpenJDK formula bottles can lag the upstream Adoptium build by patch versions, both of which introduce first-run confusion for newcomers.

The Java installer/version-manager landscape is fragmented across at least 8+ competing vendor distributions, which is a strength for redundancy but adds a selection-paradox cost for first-time installers deciding which distribution to pick.
friction_deductions.note: Small deductions applied for real observed friction rather than a full 100.

metric.installation_distribution_experie.rubric_note: Same 7-criterion weighted checklist (100 pts total) applied identically to all 10 languages in this evaluation family: (1) native OS installers Win/macOS/Linux [20], (2) system package-manager availability [20], (3) dedicated version-manager support [15], (4) official container/Docker images [15], (5) multiple independently-maintained redundant distributions [15], (6) CI/cloud integration [10], (7) documented checksum/signature verification [5].
metric.installation_distribution_experie.selection_rule_for_sampled_sources: Official Adoptium (the OpenJDK build recommended by dev.java / most-widely-adopted open-source distribution per independent guides) FAQ/docs plus vendor-neutral how-to guides covering all three major OS families (Windows, macOS, Linux) and all three installation paths (native installer, system package manager, version manager) were used as the fixed retrieval route, identical in structure to the route used for every other language's installation metric in this evaluation family.

contextual_metadata_not_scored.note_per_rubric: Language age and elapsed years are recorded here as metadata only per the frozen ecosystem rubric; they were not used as a threshold or automatic bonus/penalty in the score above.

deduction_citations: <cite index="15-9">Oracle's JDK licensing model changed several times (OTN, then NFTC, then per-employee subscription pricing), and a rich ecosystem of distributions each set its own support window.</cite>

<cite index="20-1,20-4">Oracle intends to provide Java security updates more frequently than the current quarterly CPU cadence, and plans to provide multiple monthly updates in CY27, so organizations should be preparing for this cadence.</cite>

items: Oracle's own support-cadence policy has changed multiple times (three-year to two-year LTS interval, OTN to NFTC to per-employee subscription licensing, and now a shift toward monthly Critical Security Patch Updates), which is evidence of active maturity work but also of some non-triviality in tracking which policy version currently applies to a given release.

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.rubric_note: Same 6-criterion weighted checklist (100 pts total) applied identically to all 10 languages: (1) documented predictable versioning/release scheme [20], (2) published LTS/support policy with concrete end dates [20], (3) documented backward-compatibility guarantee [20], (4) reproducible, multi-vendor supported build-artifact availability [15], (5) regular maintenance/patch cadence [15], (6) multiple independent vendors providing redundant long-term maintenance [10]. Language age/first-release date is recorded as context only and is not scored.
metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.selection_rule_for_sampled_sources: Official Oracle release-notes/support-roadmap pages, the OpenJDK project's own patch-update announcements, and independent vendor (Azul/Adoptium) and press (JRebel, ADTmag, javacodegeeks) coverage of the six-month/LTS cadence were used, matching the fixed retrieval-route structure (official primary source + vendor + independent press) applied to every other language's toolchain-stability metric in this evaluation family.
